# Mallow Standards - organisation policy index

Catalogue interface: `0.1.0-candidate.1`. **Candidate; no effective release is published by this index.**

## Start here

This is the single governance index. It routes to the existing authorities; it is not a new independent engineering policy.

- Applicability, repository classes, governance profiles and exceptions: `org-governance`.
- Normative engineering requirements and control contracts: `org-engineering-standards`.
- Shared packages and deployment tooling implement requirements; their defaults cannot redefine policy.
- Live GitHub/provider reads prove actual enforcement. Source text proves intent, not deployment or adoption.

The engineering [STANDARDS.md](https://github.com/Mallow-Dev/org-engineering-standards/blob/develop/STANDARDS.md) projection and candidate bundle provide the integrated reader/consumer view after their implementation PR lands. Until then, use the linked source documents. Never treat an open PR or mutable default-branch link as an effective immutable release.

## Source-specific boundaries

**Standards authority and precedence:** Applicability and exception decisions remain here. Pending source PR approval is not an effective engineering-policy release.

**Canonical policy/source index:** This machine-readable index is the editable authority map; Markdown and private integrated views are generated projections.

**Engineering delivery and runtime protection:** The approved engineering repository owns this requirement; current candidate wording does not establish organisation-wide adoption or operational enforcement.

**Engineering control contracts:** The approved engineering repository owns this requirement; current candidate wording does not establish organisation-wide adoption or operational enforcement.

**Repository assurance:** The approved engineering repository owns this requirement; current candidate wording does not establish organisation-wide adoption or operational enforcement.

**Release notes:** The approved engineering repository owns this requirement; current candidate wording does not establish organisation-wide adoption or operational enforcement.

**Versioning:** The approved engineering repository owns this requirement; current candidate wording does not establish organisation-wide adoption or operational enforcement.

**Time-bounded security exception engineering requirements:** The approved engineering repository owns this requirement; current candidate wording does not establish organisation-wide adoption or operational enforcement.

**Shared executable presets:** Executable configuration implements approved requirements. Local defaults and testing proposals cannot redefine normative policy.

**Deployment reference tooling:** Reference tooling is subordinate to approved governance and engineering contracts.

**Legacy branching guidance:** Retained for history and migration. Do not infer current branch routing from this document; use the approved repository declaration and live state.

**Review operating guidance:** Interpret with approved engineering review requirements and independent reviewer identity; do not silently introduce additional approval counts.

**Legacy detailed engineering guidance:** Inventory and migrate or supersede overlapping requirements in the normative engineering repository. No automatic promotion occurs here.

**Governance bootstrap templates:** Templates initialise consumers; ongoing compliance requires versioned adoption and live evidence.

**Retired classic-protection synchronisation:** The old mutation payload is retired because it contradicts live rules. No replay of obsolete approvals, check names or example exceptions is allowed.

## Other places instructions appear

| Surface | Role | Operating rule |
|---|---|---|
| Notion Mallow Standards and engineering guidance | projection | Render or link versioned sources; retain source status and verification date. Do not independently edit normative requirements. |
| Organisation discussions, issues and decision proposals | proposal | Record proposals and rationale; adopted requirements must resolve to a canonical control and approved release. |
| Repository README, CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS, agent-specific instructions and local configuration | local-declaration | Declare repository-specific facts and approved stricter requirements; reference the canonical profile and release instead of copying organisation rules. |
| Mallow skills and agent runtime | local-declaration | Skills execute applicable policy; capability visibility and instructions do not prove approval, installation or current enforcement. |
| Live GitHub rulesets, classic protection, environments and provider settings | execution-evidence | Prove actual enforcement. Reconcile drift explicitly; do not automatically treat observed state as approved desired state. |
| Durable Jobs and Durable Results | execution-evidence | Retain approved execution scope, source-bound evidence and recovery state privately. They do not independently redefine policy. |
| SharePoint locked records, Library exports and historic chats | historical | Retain dated context and supersession. Do not prefer a copied document over its canonical current source. |

## Change and adoption contract

A standards change must identify its control IDs, authority, applicability, implementation, evidence, migration impact and approval boundary. A changed index must pass `npm run standards:check`. Detailed private controls and provider snapshots remain in the private engineering repository and Durable Results, not this public repository.

Implementation state is not policy lifecycle or repository adoption. Unknown evidence stays UNKNOWN. Candidate bundles are advisory; declaring them effective is rejected by the current tooling. Human approval, source merges and formal publication remain separate gates.

The legacy classic-branch-protection synchroniser is retired. `npm run sync:protection` fails without making a network request. Its former configuration is retained in Git history, not as an actionable source. No source reconciliation authorises weakening or automatically rewriting live rulesets.
